subject: Groundline POC — on-prem K8s provisioning, network & storage acceptance
messages:
From: Alex Tomas <alex.tomas@groundline.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: On-prem cluster — initial requirements & acceptance criteria

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Groundline is ready to move to an on-prem POC at one of our regional sites. Before we kick off the procurement and rack-scheduling, we need a clear list of minimum cluster requirements, network handoff items, and acceptance criteria so our facilities and network teams can prepare. High-level asks below: 

- Expected node flavors and minimum counts for a 3-node control-plane + 3-6 worker baseline (GPU/no-GPU splits).
- Storage recommendations for model artifacts and KV caches (ephemeral NVMe for inference cache, durable SSD for artifacts).
- Storage QoS/throughput window required during peak ingest (we expect bursts up to 3GB/s for batch loads).
- Network requirements: VLAN IDs, MTU, egress IPs, firewall rules, expected BGP/peering (if any).
- KMS/HSM: we need to know whether Redwood requires a customer-managed KMS and preferred cert/key rotation cadence.
- Preflight acceptance checks (smoke tests, pod scheduling, PV attach/IO).

Can you produce a concise preflight checklist and a mutual action plan (owner + ETA per item) we can share with our infra team this week? I attached a rough site sketch.

Attachments: groundline_network_sketch.png

Alex
Alex Tomas
Head of Platform Ops, Groundline AI
alex.tomas@groundline.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC: On-prem cluster — initial requirements & acceptance criteria

Hi Alex — thanks, this is great context.

I've put together a compact preflight checklist and the node/storage baseline we recommend for a POC. Please see summary below and I attached a sample storage profile workbook with the PV size/QoS guidance.

Quick summary (POC baseline):
- Control plane: 3x m6g-like equivalents (16 vCPU / 64GB RAM) with static control-plane IPs and anti-affinity.
- Workers (inference): 3x GPU nodes (A100-ish equivalent) + 3x CPU-only for pre/post-processing. GPU nodes: 8x NVMe local (for KV cache) + 4TB SSD for models.
- Storage: 
  - Ephemeral cache: local NVMe with guaranteed IOPS (use local-block CSI for attach).
  - Durable model store: networked SSD-backed blockstore via CSI (replicated across 3 AZ-like racks).
  - Snapshot/backup: daily snapshot policy, retention 14 days for POC.
- Networking: 
  - L3 routed VLANs for control/data plane. MTU: 9000 preferred (please confirm switch support).
  - Outbound egress: provide static NAT IPs for our control-plane callbacks; 2 IPs minimum for HA.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key). Rotation cadence: we recommend 90 days for POC; can align to your policy.

Acceptance smoke tests (we can run remotely or during onsite window):
1) API smoke: 5-min chat/generation load at 200 requests/min (validate 95th latency < 250ms).
2) PV attach: provision + attach 50Gi to 10 pods concurrently; IO sanity test (fio sample).
3) KV caching: warm KV cache to confirm cache hit-rate > 80% for a 5k-token working set.
4) Failover: drain + replace one worker while routing traffic to remain within latency SLO.

Next steps I propose:
- I will share the storage profile workbook (attached) and a one-page mutual action plan by EOD.
- Can you confirm switch MTU and provide VLAN IDs and a contact for your network engineer?

Attachments: groundline_storage_profile.xlsx

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC: On-prem cluster — initial requirements & acceptance criteria

Adding some network-level details and a short handoff checklist for Groundline's infra team.

Irene's network preflight items:
- VLANs: provide IDs for control, data, mgmt, and storage. We need L3 reachability between control-plane and storage VLANs.
- MTU: 9000 recommended; if switches do not support jumbo frames we will fallback to 1500 but must know ahead to tune pod network MTU.
- Border firewall rules: open outbound ports 443 (control plane callbacks), 8443 (kube API if exposed for troubleshooting, optional), and a CIDR allowlist for our maintenance IPs (we will provide).
- BGP/peering: not required for the POC unless you want dynamic routing across racks. If you have an existing BGP fabric and prefer leveraging it, please share ASN and route-policy intent.
- NTP/DNS: ensure NTP pool access for all nodes; internal DNS zones for k8s service discovery.

Handoff items for Groundline net team (suggested owners):
- Provide VLAN IDs + switch model + MTU compliance — owner: Groundline network lead — ETA: 48 hours after this thread.
- Provide a maintenance window for net handoff (2 hour window) — owner: Groundline sched ops — ETA: next 5 business days.
- Identify a point-of-contact for firewall rule changes and provide change request process — owner: Groundline security infra.

If they can send the VLAN list and a simple L2/L3 diagram (layered with expected rack-to-rack connectivity), we can finalize the mutual action plan.

--

Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC: On-prem cluster — initial requirements & acceptance criteria

Thanks — quick notes from storage/ops perspective and proposed acceptance gates. Quoting Alex and Mina below for context.

> Mina:
> - Ephemeral cache: local NVMe with guaranteed IOPS (use local-block CSI for attach).
> - Durable model store: networked SSD-backed blockstore via CSI (replicated across 3 AZ-like racks).

Storage notes / asks:
- CSI: we will deploy csi-blockstore v1.3 (supported). Confirm Groundline's blockstore exposes the typical CSI topology keys (zone/rack). If not, we will need a thin adapter.
- Provisioning: recommend setting the PV reclaim policy to "Retain" during POC so we don't accidentally delete artifacts during teardown.
- Throughput: for the 3GB/s burst target, we need to validate per-node NIC + switch DPU capabilities. If Groundline's switches are 25G/100G we are fine; if 10G, we will constrain burst windows and use local NVMe more aggressively.
- Encryption: at-rest encryption required. We support customer-managed KMS (please share KMS admin contact and endpoint).

Proposed acceptance gates (these are binary checks we can run during the handoff window):
1) PV attach stress: 20 concurrent PV attach/detach cycles across nodes without exceeding attach latency >1s median.
2) Snapshot/restore: provision a 1TB snapshot, restore into a test PVC and run a lightweight integrity check.
3) IO throughput: run fio profile used by Redwood (attached) for 5 minutes; compare to baseline (we will share expected numbers in the preflight doc).
4) Encryption validation: test a sample object to ensure KMS-wrapped keys are used and logs show key usage.

I attached the preflight checklist we will use for validation and a network sketch for the team to align on wiring and VLANs. Once Groundline confirms VLANs + MTU + KMS point-of-contact, we can lock a 2-hour window for remote validation and a 2-day onsite support block (if needed).

Attachments: groundline_preflight_checklist.pdf, groundline_network_sketch.png

I'll also open JIRA OPS-1227 to track the handoff items and link the preflight results.

Rishi Malhotra
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
